label: cluster address family
type: the cluster-wide choice of IP address family (IPv4 or IPv6), Enterprise Edition only, changed by a changeover procedure with four preconditions: every node must be in dual-stack mode, every node must be named by a fully qualified domain name, auto-failover must be disabled, and node-to-node encryption must be disabled.
evidence: Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition supports the IPv4 and IPv6 address families.
Each cluster-node must be operating in _dual stack_ mode, thereby supporting both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.
The address family can only be changed if each cluster-node is named with a fully qualified domain-name (such as `nodename.clustername.com`).
On each node, when the address-family change occurs, all Couchbase Services hosted on that node _other than_ the Data Service are restarted.
note: The highest-precondition operation in the entire 83-page scope, and the clearest single vindication of extracting administration procedures: a cluster-wide setting with four independent preconditions, a partial service restart as a side effect, and an interaction with two other features (auto-failover, node-to-node encryption) that neither of those features' own pages mentions. None of this is derivable from a reference description of 'address family'.
